clinician.final_diagnosis: Compressive optic neuropathy (CON) of the right eye secondary to thyroid eye disease
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 66-year-old woman with longstanding hyperthyroidism and prominent goiter presented with right upper eyelid retraction. Initial blood tests demonstrated hyperthyroid state (high FT3, FT4; suppressed TSH; elevated TSAb). Orbital CT and MRI six months later showed inflammation and hypertrophy confined to the superior rectus and upper levator muscles of the right eye. This was accompanied by a significant reduction in corrected visual acuity to 20/200 and a decreased central critical flicker fusion frequency of 16 Hz in the right eye, confirming compressive optic neuropathy.
